checklists.title: Restore stock firmware
checklists.summary: Return the phone to the exact firmware that shipped for its model and region.
checklists.warning: A firmware package for another model, region, or carrier can brick the phone or wipe its radio calibration.

items.title: Confirm the exact model and codename
items.detail: Open Settings > About phone and compare the model number with the firmware package. Codename mismatches are a common cause of hard bricks.

items.title: Use an official firmware source
items.detail: Download from the manufacturer's support page or a signed OTA package. Avoid file-sharing mirrors and pre-rooted firmware.

items.title: Check region and carrier code
items.detail: Samsung CSC, Xiaomi region, and carrier variants must match. A different CSC may flash but lose VoLTE or updates.

items.title: Back up photos, messages, and authenticators
items.detail: Most restore methods erase user data. Copy the backup to another disk, not only to the phone.

items.title: Charge the phone above 60%
items.detail: A power loss in the middle of a flash is one of the few ways to create a real brick.

items.title: Install the official USB driver and test the cable
items.detail: Use a data-capable cable and a rear USB port. Confirm the phone appears in Device Manager or with adb devices.

items.title: Close other phone tools
items.detail: Samsung Smart Switch, Xiaomi Assistant, and virtual machines can claim the USB device while you flash.

items.title: Read the restore steps twice
items.detail: Know which slot or partition is being written and what the tool will do when it finishes.

items.title: Never unplug during the write
items.detail: Wait for the tool to report success and for the phone to reboot on its own before touching the cable.

checklists.title: Unlock the bootloader
checklists.summary: Remove the bootloader lock so a custom recovery or boot image can be installed.
checklists.warning: Unlocking usually wipes all user data, voids the warranty, and may disable DRM, banking apps, or OTA updates.

items.title: Verify that you own the device
items.detail: Never unlock a phone that is financed, reported stolen, or owned by someone else. The unlock may be irreversible.

items.title: Back up everything first
items.detail: The unlock command normally performs a factory reset. Copy the backup off the phone before starting.

items.title: Enable OEM unlocking and USB debugging
items.detail: Both switches are in Developer options. Enable Developer options by tapping the build number seven times.

items.title: Meet the manufacturer's waiting period
items.detail: Xiaomi, Huawei, and some carriers require a signed-in account for several days before allowing the unlock.

items.title: Install official Platform Tools
items.detail: Use Google's official ADB and Fastboot package. Confirm that adb devices lists the phone with an authorized state.

items.title: Charge above 60%
items.detail: The unlock sequence reboots the phone more than once and must not lose power.

items.title: Run the manufacturer-approved unlock
items.detail: Use fastboot flashing unlock, fastboot oem unlock, or the official vendor tool. Read the on-screen warning before confirming.

items.title: Confirm the bootloader state
items.detail: Run fastboot getvar unlocked or read the boot screen. Do not continue while the device still reports locked.

items.title: Review what stopped working
items.detail: Some banking, payment, and streaming apps refuse to run. Decide before unlocking whether that is acceptable.

checklists.title: Install a custom recovery
checklists.summary: Flash TWRP or OrangeFox to create backups and install community packages.
checklists.warning: A recovery image for a different model can cause a bootloop. Encryption support varies by build.

items.title: Confirm the bootloader is unlocked
items.detail: Most phones refuse to flash a recovery while the bootloader is locked.

items.title: Match the exact codename
items.detail: Recovery builds are device-specific. A build for a similar model is still the wrong build.

items.title: Download from the official project
items.detail: Use twrp.me or orangefox.download. Check whether the build is marked official or unofficial.

items.title: Verify the image checksum
items.detail: Compare the file hash with the value published by the maintainer before flashing.

items.title: Back up the current boot image
items.detail: A stock boot image lets you recover from a bad recovery flash or a later root attempt.

items.title: Test Fastboot before flashing
items.detail: Run fastboot devices and confirm the serial number. Fix driver problems before writing anything.

items.title: Charge above 60%
items.detail: Recovery installation is short, but the first boot and backup can take much longer.

items.title: Boot directly into recovery
items.detail: Some stock ROMs restore the stock recovery on boot. Boot into the new recovery immediately after flashing.

items.title: Create a full recovery backup
items.detail: Back up boot, system, data, and vendor partitions to an external drive if the recovery supports it.

checklists.title: Root the phone
checklists.summary: Patch the boot image with Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch and verify root access.
checklists.warning: Root weakens the security model, voids warranties, and can leave the phone unbootable if the wrong image is patched.

items.title: Confirm the bootloader is unlocked
items.detail: Rooting a locked phone normally requires an exploit. DroidCrate does not provide exploits or bypasses.

items.title: Match the boot image to the installed firmware
items.detail: A boot image from another build or region can fail to boot. Check the build number in Settings.

items.title: Use the official root project
items.detail: Download Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch from its official GitHub releases or website.

items.title: Keep an untouched boot image
items.detail: Store the original boot.img somewhere safe. It is your fastest way back to a bootable phone.

items.title: Patch the image with the manager app
items.detail: Follow the official installation guide. Do not flash a pre-patched image from a stranger.

items.title: Flash or boot the patched image
items.detail: Prefer fastboot boot for a first test when supported. Flash only after the temporary boot succeeds.

items.title: Verify root and module support
items.detail: Open the manager, confirm the installed version, and test one small module before installing more.

items.title: Configure the deny list
items.detail: Hide root from banking and payment apps only after confirming the device is stable.

items.title: Plan for OTA updates
items.detail: System updates usually remove root. Keep the stock boot image and repeat the patch after each update.

checklists.title: Install a custom ROM
checklists.summary: Replace the stock system with a community build for the same device codename.
checklists.warning: A custom ROM wipes data and can break the camera, VoLTE, or safety certifications. Anti-rollback can make downgrades impossible.

items.title: Confirm the ROM supports your exact codename
items.detail: The maintainer page must list your model. Marketing names are not enough.

items.title: Read the full maintainer notes
items.detail: Check the required firmware base, known bugs, and whether a clean flash is mandatory.

items.title: Install the required stock firmware first
items.detail: Many ROMs require a specific vendor or firmware version before installation.

items.title: Install a compatible custom recovery
items.detail: Use the recovery version recommended by the ROM maintainer, not an arbitrary newer build.

items.title: Back up the entire phone
items.detail: Copy photos, messages, authenticators, and the stock boot image to another device.

items.title: Charge above 60%
items.detail: First boot and data migration can take a long time. Do not let the phone die mid-install.

items.title: Download the matching extras
items.detail: Use only the GApps, vendor, and firmware packages named in the ROM instructions.

items.title: Format data when the ROM requires it
items.detail: Encrypted data from the stock ROM often prevents the new system from booting.

items.title: Keep the stock firmware package
items.detail: You need it to return to a supported state, restore VoLTE, or recover from a failed boot.

items.title: Record the IMEI and back up the modem
items.detail: Note the IMEI from the box or Settings. Never use tools that promise to rewrite or repair an IMEI.
